title: Fabrication of mixed-valence Cu species supported on rice husk ash-derived silica for efficient 4-nitrophenol reduction
content: The persistence and environmental risks of organic contaminants in industrial wastewater have motivated continued research into development of effective and sustainable catalysts for their removal. Herein, a copper-based catalyst supported on rice husk ash (RHA)-derived silica was synthesized via a facile and efficient impregnation–calcination procedure, exhibiting exceptional catalytic activity toward the NaBH4-assisted reduction of 4-nitrophenol (4-NP), a model organic pollutant. A series of catalysts with varying Cu loadings were prepared and comprehensively characterized using advanced physicochemical techniques (FTIR, XRD, H2-TPR, BET, SEM–EDS mapping, XPS, XRF, and TEM). The characterization results confirmed the successful synthesis of SiO2 and the incorporation of Cu species into the SiO2 support to form the catalyst. Cu loadings ranging from 12 to 24 wt% were investigated, among which 16Cu/Si exhibited relatively high reducibility, limited particle agglomeration, and a specific surface area of 147.9 m2 g−1. Under optimized conditions, nearly 100% catalytic removal of 4-NP by the 16Cu/Si catalyst in the presence of NaBH4 was achieved within 10 min. Post-reaction characterization of the spent catalyst revealed that the structural framework was largely preserved, accompanied by partial reduction of the Cu-based active sites to lower-valent Cu species. Furthermore, the 16Cu/Si sample exhibited excellent stability over eleven consecutive cycles. Overall, this study highlights the potential of RHA-derived silica for developing sustainable, high-performance heterogeneous catalysts for reduction reactions via a facile synthesis route.
